heroHeadline: Day 577: Sheinbaum Dispatches Top Security Officials to Sinaloa; Rocha Moya Steps Down; Workers' Day 40-Hour Workweek Signed; Morena Elects Ariadna Montiel
heroSubtitle: The week of May 1–4, 2026 saw Mexico navigate its most acute sovereignty dual-crisis in recent history while also marking major domestic milestones. On May 1 (Workers' Day), Sheinbaum held a People's Mañanera at the Centro Cultural del México Contemporáneo, signing a phased 40-hour workweek agreement (to take full effect by 2030) and naming agronomist Columba Jasmin López as the new Agriculture Secretary (replacing Julio Berdegué). She announced private investment simplification measures and defended government gasoline price caps with oil at ~$120/barrel. On the Sinaloa sovereignty front, she was blunt: 'There is a principle called sovereignty, and that isn't negotiated.' On May 2, Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya submitted a formal 30-day leave request via video message; the state congress approved and installed Yeraldine Bonilla Valverde as the first female interim governor of Sinaloa. Culiacán Mayor Gámez Mendívil also stepped down. Mexico's FGR announced insufficient evidence for extradition detention. On May 4, Sheinbaum confirmed she had dispatched Public Safety Secretary García Harfuch and Defense Secretary Ricardo Trevilla Trejo directly to Sinaloa to coordinate with the interim government — a federal stabilization operation for Mexico's most security-challenged state. The Morena National Council meeting over the weekend elected Ariadna Montiel Reyes as Morena's new National President, replacing Luisa María Alcalde who moved to the Executive Legal Office. The first formal USMCA negotiating round remains on track for the week of May 25 in Mexico City.
